issues.failure_explanation: Part 1 asserts E||(u,v)_t-(u,v)_s||^q < c|t-s|^{q/2}. The proof treats the singular drift 1/u by Hölder with exponents (2-ε,(2-ε)/(1-ε)). This gives the factor |t-s|^{(1-ε)/(2-ε)}, which is strictly smaller than 1/2 for ε>0, and the proof ends with |t-s|^{1/2-ε}. The exact q/2 rate is not proved. Part 2 then uses 'O(|t-s|^{(1-ε)p/2}) by part 1' and 'O(|t-s|^{ε/2})' with the sharp exponent. The claimed rate is plausible via the Cartesian lift, since u=|(y,z)| is 1-Lipschitz in (y,z), but that argument is not given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove part 1 via the Cartesian SDE (cyl), where the drift has linear growth and |u_t-u_s| ≤ |(y,z)_t-(y,z)_s|. Alternatively state part 1 with the exponent actually obtained and re-track exponents in part 2.
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 of timeregbnd and the residual estimates r_{1,k}, r_{2,k} in the strong-convergence proof use the unproved sharp exponent. The final rate Δt^{1/2-ε} is probably unchanged after re-tracking the exponents.
issues.title: Increment bound claimed with rate |t-s|^{q/2} but proof only yields a worse exponent
issues.why_classification: A short local argument or exponent bookkeeping restores the statement, and the final 1/2-ε rate survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it is enough to find an $\epsilon>0$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T]$

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed claim is E exp(γ∫_0^T ||b(z_s)||^2 ds)<∞ for every T>0 and every γ>0. The proof needs α=2εγB^2<βλ, so it only bounds the exponential moment over windows of length ε<βλ/(2γB^2), which shrinks as γ grows. This suffices for Novikov via the sub-interval criterion with the single value γ=β/4. It does not give the stated global-in-time bound for arbitrary γ. For an OU-type process E exp(γ∫_0^T |z|^2) is infinite once γT is large, so the unrestricted claim is not supported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma as the Novikov condition (γ=β/4, or exponential integrability over sufficiently short windows depending on γ).
issues.overall_effect: Only the stated generality is affected. The Girsanov argument for u_t>0 and the strong Feller property uses the local-in-time Novikov criterion with a fixed γ, which the proof does support.
issues.title: Novikov lemma stated for all T and all γ but proved only on short intervals with γ-dependent length
issues.why_classification: Restating the lemma at the scope actually proved keeps the downstream use intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: as it is a bounded perturbation (given by $G$) of a convex potential (given by $\frac12\lambda\|\vec x\|^2$)

issues.failure_explanation: The target is π ∝ exp(-β(λ|x|²/2+G_3)). Bakry–Émery gives the LSI constant βλ for the Gaussian part. The perturbation is βG_3, with oscillation β(sup G-inf G). Holley–Stroock therefore gives R=βλ·exp(-β(sup G-inf G)), not βλ·exp(inf G-sup G). The stated R is too large for β>1, so the claimed exponential rate exp(-2Rt/β) is not justified. The proof also drops the factor H(ρ_0|π) in 'H(p(t)|π)≤exp(-2Rt/β)'.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace R by βλ·exp(-β(sup G-inf G)) and restore the factor H(ρ_0|π) in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit contraction rate in (hhh) is wrong for β≠1. Geometric convergence in entropy still holds with the corrected constant.
issues.title: Holley–Stroock rate in Theorem thm_bndd_G omits the factor β in the exponent
issues.why_classification: Only a constant changes, and the qualitative geometric convergence claim is preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Minimizing the right-hand side with respect to $\delta$

issues.failure_explanation: The function to minimise is (2A/p)(δ2^{p-1}+(p-1)δ^{-1/(p-1)}R^{-p}). Its minimiser is δ^{-1}=R^{p-1}2^{(p-1)/p}, not R^{p-1}2^{p-2+1/p}. The minimum value is (2A/p)R^{-(p-1)}(2^{(p-1)^2/p}+(p-1)2^{1/p}). For p=3 this is about 3.36 A R^{-2}, whereas the stated bound 2A R^{-p+1}2^{1-1/p} is about 3.17 A R^{-2}. The displayed final bound is therefore not what the argument yields for p>2. The two expressions coincide only at p=2.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit tail constant in the stated estimate is wrong. The term still decays like R^{-(p-1)}, so the conclusion E sup||e||→0 is unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:num_conv is a statement for one fixed initial law ρ_0 with ρ_0/π bounded. All constants (Corollary cor, timeregbnd, ass:2) depend on ‖ρ_0/π‖ and on moments of ρ_0, and the stopped-error bound carries exp(2TC_R). In the invariant-measure proof the initial law is π̃_Δt, which changes with Δt, and the ball radius is R=Δt^{-1}→∞. Neither the boundedness of π̃_Δt/π nor uniformity in Δt of ‖π̃_Δt/π‖_{L^p(π)} and of the error constants is shown, so E_{1,T}(Δt)→0 does not follow. The quantity E_{1,T} as defined equals π̃_Δt(P_Tφ)-π̃_Δt(φ). Since π̃_Δt is not invariant for the chain, this is not the numerical-versus-exact discrepancy to which thm:num_conv applies. The final line also writes '|π_Δt(φ)-π(φ)|=ε' instead of ≤ε. The preamble cites thm_bndd_G, which needs bounded G, while the proof uses erg2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, one must either prove uniform-in-Δt control of the initial laws (density ratio w.r.t. π and tail/moment bounds) together with uniform constants in the finite-time error estimate, or obtain uniform-in-Δt geometric ergodicity of the numerical chain and use a fixed initial law.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised result that the stationary law of the scheme converges to π as Δt→0 is not established. The argument needs convergence uniform over a family of initial laws that vary with Δt.
issues.title: Convergence of the numerical invariant measure: finite-time error theorem applied with Δt-dependent initial laws without uniformity
issues.why_classification: Any fix needs a new uniform-in-initial-data error estimate or uniform ergodicity of the scheme, which is a new lemma-level construction; the paper's claimed convergence of the invariant measure is unsupported until then.
